parsed.summary: For every natural p ≥ 1 the Lean statement asserts an equivalent norm N on real ℓ¹(ℕ) such that (1/2)‖c‖₁ ≤ N(c) ≤ B_p‖c‖₁, where B_p = 300p²+150p+5. With that norm and the original vector-space operations, ℓ¹ is complete, has 2B_p-BAP and fails p-BAP. For p = 1 it fails 1-BAP, i.e. MAP. This matches Corollary 1.3 faithfully. The main caveat is minor: the statement depends on the local `letI` instances for the norm N, rather than the global ℓ¹ instances, being the ones picked up inside `HasBAP` and `CompleteSpace`. Lean prioritises local instances, so this should be fine.

glossary.plain: X has the Λ-bounded approximation property. For every compact C ⊆ X and ε > 0 there is a bounded linear T: X → X with finite-dimensional range, ‖T‖ ≤ Λ, and sup_{u∈C} ‖Tu − u‖ ≤ η for some η < ε.
glossary.note: Writing the bound as ≤ η for some η < ε is equivalent to a strict uniform bound < ε on C.

glossary.plain: Real ℓ¹(ℕ) with its usual norm ‖·‖₁
Statement of Corollary 1.3: an equivalent renorming of ℓ¹ with the stated bounds, keeping the module structure fixed, that is complete, has 2B_p-BAP, fails p-BAP, and for p = 1 fails MAP.

lean_claims.plain: For every natural p ≥ 1 there is an additive group norm N on ℓ¹(ℕ) with the following properties. (1) N(rc) = |r|N(c). (2) (1/2)‖c‖₁ ≤ N(c) ≤ B_p‖c‖₁ for all c. (3) There is a normed-space structure for N extending the original ℝ-module structure under which ℓ¹ is complete, has 2B_p-BAP, fails p-BAP, and, if p = 1, fails 1-BAP.

paper_claims.plain: For each integer p ≥ 1, real ℓ¹ has an equivalent norm ‖·‖_p with (1/2)‖c‖₁ ≤ ‖c‖_p ≤ B_p‖c‖₁. Under it, ℓ¹ has 2B_p-BAP but fails p-BAP; for p = 1 the norm fails MAP.
There is a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose free space has AP but fails BAP.
Finite anchor obstruction for each block M_p.

coverage.why: All bounds, BAP constants and the MAP failure for p = 1 match; the module operations are kept fixed.
Free spaces are not formalized in this file.

flags.explanation: Correctness depends on the local `letI` instances (norm N and structure s) being used inside `HasBAP` and `CompleteSpace`, overriding the global ℓ¹ instances declared at lines 30-34. Lean 4 prefers local instances, so this is very likely fine. If the global instance were used instead, the BAP claims would concern the original ℓ¹ norm, which has MAP; the statement would then be contradictory rather than vacuous.
